name: Appenzell iodized-salt distribution
description: Hans Eggenberger and colleagues promoted iodized salt in Appenzell Ausserrhoden as a population nutrition measure.

date.basis: Date refers to this scoped event or archaeological context, not to a global origin.

events.statement: Hans Eggenberger and colleagues promoted iodized salt in Appenzell Ausserrhoden as a population nutrition measure.

evidence.supports: The federal expert report describes Hans Eggenberger’s 1922 campaign in Appenzell Ausserrhoden, a petition with 3,480 signatures, cantonal approval and iodized salt distribution. It also describes earlier work by Otto Bayard and a later national recommendation; signatures are not consumers or coverage.
This 2002 review reports Eggenberger’s 1922 Appenzell Ausserrhoden petition of 3,480 signatures and subsequent authorization for sale of iodized salt. Signatures are not a count of consumers.

events.caveats: Other investigators and earlier local initiatives preceded this campaign. A petition count is not proof that all residents consumed the salt.
